title: $L^1(\mu)$ integrability and normalization of the candidate density $R_\psi$

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Sub-lemma (GAP 2).** With the heuristic density

$$R_\psi(u)=\exp\Big(\langle\psi,u\rangle_{CM}-\tfrac12\|\psi\|_{CM}^2-\tfrac{\lambda}{4}\big[-4\!\int\!:\!u^3\!:\psi+6\!\int\!:\!u^2\!:\psi^2-4\!\int\! u\psi^3+\!\int\!\psi^4\big]\Big),$$

prove $R_\psi\in L^1(\mu)$ and $\int R_\psi\,d\mu=1$; ideally $R_\psi\in L^{1+\epsilon}(\mu)$.

**Why nontrivial.** The Cameron–Martin term $\langle\psi,u\rangle_{CM}$ and the renormalized **cubic** term $\int :\!u^3\!:\psi$ have heavy tails. Exponential integrability does NOT hold for the GFF; it can only hold for $\Phi^4_3$ because the quartic confinement $-\tfrac{\lambda}4\int u^4$ in $\mu$ dominates the cubic growth. The proof must invoke sharp $\Phi^4_3$ tail estimates (Barashkov–Gubinelli sub-Gaussian tails; Hairer–Steele 2022) to close the integrability bound. Normalization $\int R_\psi d\mu=1$ is needed to make $R_\psi$ a genuine Radon–Nikodym derivative.

**Deliverable.** A complete exponential-moment estimate showing $\mathbb{E}_\mu[R_\psi^{1+\epsilon}]<\infty$, with the cubic term controlled by the quartic confinement, plus the normalization identity.
